pages.text: Snow fell overnight. It was knee-deep in the alley, too deep to run through.
Nono wanted to race with his friends. He brought out a broom.
He swept the snow in front of him. The stone paving appeared.
Beside the swept patch lay untouched white snow. Nono dropped the broom and drew in it.
He drew circle after circle. Half the alley was still covered in snow.
All three started their race. Their feet sank into the snow.
They tried again. Their feet sank again. They could not race.
Grandpa Badger said, "Someone swept half the snow, then went off to play. Now the snow will stay all day."
Nono picked up the broom again. This time he swept all the way to the end.
The stone paving was clear. All three ran happily to the end of the alley.
